url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

Below is a step‑by‑step guide to build the **GET** request that will return the *Speed* information for a specific interface on a Cisco Nexus Dashboard (ND) instance. | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Base URL** | `https://192.120.45.67` | | **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Query Parameters** | `fabricName=Network1`
`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=Ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json`
`Content-Type: application/json` | > **NOTE** > Replace `` with a valid bearer token that you obtain from ND’s authentication service (e.g., via OAuth2 or a static token). > If you’re using a self‑signed certificate, you may need to add `-k` (curl) or `verify=False` (Python) to skip SSL verification. --- ## 1. Build the full URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` --- ## 2. Example Requests ### a) Using `curl` ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` ### b) Using Python (`requests`) ```python import requests url = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" params = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "Ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer ", "Accept": "application/json", "Content-Type": "application/json" } response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, verify=False) # verify=False if using self‑signed cert print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` --- ## 3. Using the Provided Tool (`functions.requests_get`) If you want to let the assistant actually perform the request (assuming the tool has access to the ND instance), you can invoke the function like this: ```json { "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", "params": { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "Ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } } ``` > **Caution** – The tool will not automatically add the `Authorization` header. If the tool requires it, you’ll need to pass it as part of the `params` or modify the tool’s implementation accordingly. --- ## 4. What to Expect A successful response (HTTP 200) will contain JSON similar to: ```json { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "Ethernet", "infoType": "Speed", "speedMbps": 1000 } ``` If the interface does not exist or the parameters are wrong, you’ll receive an error code (e.g., 404 or 400) with a descriptive message. --- ### Quick Checklist | ✅ | Item | |----|------| | ✅ | Base URL + Endpoint | | ✅ | Query parameters | | ✅ | Authorization header | | ✅ | Accept / Content‑Type headers | | ✅ | Correct HTTP method (GET) | | ✅ | Handle SSL verification if needed | That’s all you need to generate and execute a RESTful API request to fetch the speed of an Ethernet interface on Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy querying!
